{{Short description|American mechanical engineer (born 1939)}}
'''Francis Charles Moon''' (born 1939) is an American mechanical engineer.

Moon earned his [[bachelor's degree|bachelor's]] and [[master's degree|master's]] degrees in mechanical engineering from the [[Pratt Institute]] in 1962 and 1964, respectively, then completed his doctoral studies at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="cueng">{{cite news |title=Francis Charles Moon |url=https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/francis-charles-moon/ |access-date=24 September 2023 |publisher=Sibley College and School of Mechanical Engineering, Cornell University}}</ref> He later joined Cornell's faculty, succeeding [[Yih-Hsing Pao]] as chair of the Department of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics from 1980 to 1987, then serving as director of  Sibley School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at Cornell University until 1992.<ref name="sshist">{{cite news |last1=Moon |first1=Francis C. |title=A Brief History of the Sibley College and School |url=https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/mae/about/history-sibley-college-school/ |access-date=24 September 2023 |publisher=Sibley College and School of Mechanical Engineering, Cornell University |date=15 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Moon, Francis C. |url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/collections/3bf85274-5030-448b-a64f-b8bb8c0847f3 |access-date=24 September 2023 |publisher=Cornell University Library}}</ref> Moon was also Joseph C. Ford Professor of Engineering, and was awarded emeritus status upon retirement.<ref name="cueng"/>

Moon was honored with the 2011 [[Robert Henry Thurston Lecture Award]] from the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]].<ref name="asme">{{cite web |title=Robert Henry Thurston Lecture Award |publisher=American Society of Mechanical Engineers |url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/robert-henry-thurston-lecture-award |access-date=June 14, 2026}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] in 1996, "[f]or experimental research in chaotic and nonlinear dynamics and development of superconducting levitation devices."<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. Francis Charles Moon |url=https://www.nae.edu/29858/Dr-Francis-Charles-Moon |access-date=24 September 2023 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
